title: RBC celebrates Canadian women entrepreneurs
description: Canada is home to 1.4 million women entrepreneurs with businesses that generate $117 billion in economic activity a year. We asked successful Canadian female entrepreneurs to share their stories and offer advice on how to support aspiring female business owners get ahead.

asr.full_text: Music Dr. I am glad to change peoples definition of what a young, successful entrepreneurial woman looks like. I had to prove to people that I was worthy of the position. At the age of 53 years old I decided to go in a new venture and open my first restaurant. I'm proud to get up every morning and to give over 300 people a job. Can I do this? Can I launch this business? Do I have the support and the resources and the tools? There's so many reasons why women believe they can't do it, which is why they don't do it. CHUNLIN WANG CHAPCHUNNANJIA It doesn't matter what industry you're in. As an entrepreneur, I'm sure that we have some common challenges. KELLEY CHENG We're still in a process of building up where we are in the world. If you love your daughter, your niece, your sister, don't just bring them to the ballroom and teach them how to dance. Take them into the boardroom to teach them how business is run. I see so many more invitations for mentoring and network conversations in the past few years than I've had in my entire career. The success I've seen both as an Olympic athlete and as a business owner I know has come from the mentors in my life who have believed in me first. Supporting women is not just about the women, it's supporting everyone here in the country. When women truly find their voice, their real true authentic voice, they become unstoppable. We're all in this together. When women are successful, when women are successful, when women are successful we are all successful. I truly believe that.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents an RBC-branded interview feature about women entrepreneurs, their experiences, mentoring, and encouragement for aspiring business owners. The $117 billion figure is an economic-activity statistic, not a promised investment return, guaranteed income, or participation condition, and the closing branding reinforces an inclusion and support theme.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central content is business education and discussion through entrepreneur interviews, advice about how business is run, and discussion of mentoring and networking. No scam mechanism or paid earning guidance is evidenced.
